```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PCP-004"
UO = "harvest"
UO_TITLE = "Harvest and Clarification (Step 4)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ------------------
HARV = CFG.unit_op(UO)
p_cent = HARV.param("centrifuge_g")          # centrifugation intensity (settable)
p_load = HARV.param("depth_filter_load")     # depth filter load (settable)
p_turb = HARV.param("turbidity")             # post-clarification turbidity (outcome)
SET_PARAMS = [p_cent, p_load]                # the directly settable inputs
LEVELS = ("low characterization edge", "set-point", "high characterization edge")
n_conditions = len(SET_PARAMS) * len(LEVELS)

def setp(p):
    return f"{p.setpoint:g} {p.unit}"

def par_span(p):
    return f"{p.prange[0]:g} to {p.prange[1]:g} {p.unit}"

def nor_span(p):
    return f"{p.nor[0]:g} to {p.nor[1]:g} {p.unit}"

def area(x):
    return f"{x:,.0f} m2"

# platform step recovery and the recovery decision floor (mean less three SD)
y_base = HARV.raw["yield"]["base"]
y_cv = HARV.raw["yield"]["cv"]
y_floor = y_base * (1 - 3 * y_cv)

# impurity burden the step carries forward, and the clearance the train must deliver
hcp_broth = CFG.unit_op("bioreactor").raw["rsm"]["harvest_centre"]["hcp"]
hcp_ds_limit = float(cqa_reg.loc[cqa_reg.key == "hcp", "acc_high"].iloc[0])
hcp_logs = np.log10(hcp_broth / hcp_ds_limit)

# commercial-scale filtration duty implied by the load parameter
scale_l = V["commercial_scale_l"]
area_sp = scale_l / p_load.setpoint
area_lo = scale_l / p_load.nor[1]
area_hi = scale_l / p_load.nor[0]
turb_loq_x = p_turb.nor[1] / amv_3015_loq

# planned univariate condition list
cond_rows = []
for _p in SET_PARAMS:
    _other = [q for q in SET_PARAMS if q.key != _p.key][0]
    cond_rows.append([_p.name, _p.unit, f"{_p.prange[0]:g}", f"{_p.setpoint:g}",
                      f"{_p.prange[1]:g}", f"{_other.name} at {_other.setpoint:g} {_other.unit}"])
cond_df = pd.DataFrame(cond_rows, columns=["Parameter varied", "Unit", "Low edge",
                                           "Set-point", "High edge", "Other parameter held at"])

# planned acceptance and decision criteria
acc_df = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Post-clarification turbidity", "Nephelometry (AMV-3015)",
     f"Within the normal operating range of {nor_span(p_turb)} at the set-point condition; "
     f"reported without a limit at the other conditions"],
    ["Product recovery over the step", "Mass balance from volume and protein concentration",
     f"Mean not below {pct(y_floor)} of the product mass entering the step"],
    ["Depth filter train pressure", "In-process differential pressure",
     "Batch volume completed without exceeding the media manufacturer's rated "
     "differential pressure"],
    ["Aggregates (HMW)", "SEC-HPLC (AMV-3011)",
     "No increase across the step beyond the precision of the method"],
    ["Host cell protein and residual DNA", "ELISA (AMV-3012); qPCR (AMV-3014)",
     "Characterized and reported as the capture feed; no limit applied at this step"],
], columns=["Attribute or outcome", "Method or basis", "Criterion for a studied condition"])
```

# Purpose and scope

Harvest and clarification is the primary recovery step of the A-Mab drug substance
process, and this plan defines the studies that will characterize it. The step separates
the antibody from cells and cell debris, and it delivers the clarified harvest that the
Protein A capture step (Step 5) receives. It forms no product quality attribute of its
own, and its parameters exist for two purposes: to make the product recovery
reproducible, and to keep the composition of the material handed to capture consistent
from batch to batch.

The scope covers the three parameters listed in @tbl-params, studied at a qualified
scale-down model of the commercial harvest train (SOP-1001). Centrifugation intensity
(rcf) and depth filter load are the two settable inputs. Post-clarification turbidity is
the attribute by which the clarified harvest is released to capture, and its range is in
scope because it defines the feed that the capture step has to accept.

The plan does not cover the fed-batch culture that produces the broth, which is
characterized under PCP-003. It does not cover the capture step, which is characterized
under PCP-005. No viral clearance is claimed for harvest and clarification, and no log
reduction will be measured across it.

The work is Stage 1 process design under the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011], and it follows the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8, ICH Q9 and ICH
Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. The methodology, the attribute framework and the
parameter classification scheme are those of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The
studies support the transfer of the drug substance process from the sending site to the
receiving site under PTP-001.

# Objectives

The study has five objectives.

- To establish the effect of centrifugation intensity on centrate clarity, on product
  recovery, and on the impurity burden released into the centrate by cell lysis (HCP and
  residual DNA).
- To establish the effect of depth filter load on filtrate turbidity, on the differential
  pressure of the filter train, and on product recovery.
- To confirm that the size variant profile of the antibody (high molecular weight species
  by SEC-HPLC) does not change across the step over the ranges studied.
- To characterize the host cell protein (HCP) and residual DNA burden of the clarified
  harvest, which is the input the capture step has to clear.
- To propose a proven acceptable range and a normal operating range for each parameter,
  and to support the classification of each parameter under SOP-4001.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

Harvest and clarification is a platform operation at Novacyte Biologics, so the study
confirms and bounds behaviour that is already understood. The same continuous disk-stack
centrifuge and the same graded depth filter train have been used for three previous
humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and for the A-Mab clinical campaigns.
Across those products the step has consistently delivered clarified harvest of acceptable
turbidity and consistent recovery. This experience reduces the work required here to a
confirmation of the proposed ranges at the commercial scale-down model.

@tbl-train places the step in the drug substance train. Step 4 sits between the
production bioreactor (Step 3), which forms the glycan, charge variant and aggregate
attributes, and the capture step (Step 5), which begins the removal of process
impurities. The clarified harvest is the only material transferred between them.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(process_steps_df())
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug substance process train and the principal role of each step. {#tbl-train}")
```

The two settable parameters act through different mechanisms, and each one carries a
penalty at the end of its range. Centrifugation removes cells and large debris by
sedimentation, so a higher relative centrifugal force gives a clearer centrate. Higher
force also raises the hydrodynamic shear in the feed zone and at the solids discharge
(the two places at which the broth is accelerated most sharply), which breaks a fraction
of the cells and releases HCP, DNA and fine particles into the centrate. The two effects
oppose each other, and the set-point is expected to lie near the force at which the gain
in clarity no longer pays for the additional lysis.

Depth filtration retains the fine particles that the centrifuge does not remove. Its
capacity is expressed as the volume filtered per unit of media area
(`{python} p_load.unit`), and both the
filtrate turbidity and the differential pressure rise as that load increases. Loading
beyond the capacity of the primary media allows fines to break through into the filtrate,
which raises the turbidity of the clarified harvest and increases the particulate burden
carried into the capture column, and both of those effects are expected at the high end
of the load range studied here. The depth filter media also adsorb a fraction of the HCP
and the DNA in the centrate (an effect seen across the platform products). That clearance
varies with the state of the culture at harvest and is not predictable, so none is
claimed for this step.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step sets no critical quality attribute. The attributes in scope are the ones it
carries forward to the purification train (@tbl-cqa), and they are given there with their
drug substance acceptance criteria and their criticality.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["hcp", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw"]))
print()
print(": Quality attributes carried forward from harvest and clarification. The step "
      "forms none of them and is credited with no clearance of them. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

Host cell protein is the attribute in this table that most constrains the design of the
downstream train. The clarified harvest is expected to carry about
`{python} f"{hcp_broth:,.0f}"` ng/mg of HCP against a drug substance limit of
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_limit:g}"` ng/mg, so the purification train has to deliver about
`{python} f"{hcp_logs:.1f}"` logs of clearance in total, of which the capture step
provides the largest single contribution (PCR-005) and the two ion exchange polishing
steps provide the remainder (PCR-007 and PCR-008). Harvest and clarification is credited
with none of it. What the step does control is the consistency of the burden it hands
over, which is why HCP and residual DNA are measured on the clarified harvest at every
studied condition.

The size variant profile is measured for a different reason. Shear at the centrifuge feed
zone is the only mechanism at this step that could raise the level of high molecular
weight species, and the study measures aggregate across the step to confirm that it does
not. Aggregate reduction is the business of the cation exchange step (PCR-007), and none
is expected or claimed here.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 assigned a study type to every parameter in the drug substance train
(`{python} V['n_parameters']` parameters in total), and all three harvest parameters were
assigned to univariate study. Neither settable parameter is linked to a critical quality
attribute, and no interaction between them is expected to act on product quality, so
neither reached the risk score at which a multivariate design is required. The assigned
study type is carried into the last column of @tbl-params.

The characterization ranges are wider than the routine control ranges, so that the study
bounds the consequence of an excursion as well as the behaviour at the set-point. The
centrifugation range spans `{python} par_span(p_cent)` against a normal operating range
of `{python} nor_span(p_cent)`. The depth filter load range spans
`{python} par_span(p_load)` against a normal operating range of
`{python} nor_span(p_load)`. Turbidity is studied to `{python} f"{p_turb.prange[1]:g}"`
NTU (AMV-3015), which is twice the upper edge of its normal operating range, because the
capture step has to be shown to tolerate a harvest at the worst clarity that the
clarification train can produce.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The studies will be run at a scale-down model of the commercial harvest train, qualified
before the first characterization run (SOP-1001). The model uses a bench continuous
disk-stack centrifuge matched to the commercial machine on equivalent settling area and
on feed residence time, followed by a depth filter train of the same media grades in the
same sequence, operated at the same volume per unit of media area. Scale-independent
settings (relative centrifugal force, load per unit area, temperature) will be held at
the values proposed for commercial operation. Scale-dependent settings (feed flow rate,
solids discharge interval, hold-up volumes) will be established so that the model matches
the performance of the commercial train.

At commercial scale the filtration duty follows from the load parameter and the batch
volume. A working volume of `{python} f"{scale_l:,.0f}"` L (the commercial bioreactor
volume) at the set-point load of `{python} setp(p_load)` calls for about
`{python} area(area_sp)` of depth filter media, and the normal operating range
corresponds to about `{python} f"{area_lo:,.0f}"` to `{python} area(area_hi)`. The scale-down
model is operated at the same volume per unit area, so the duty on the media is preserved
even though the absolute area is not.

Qualification will use triplicate model runs on a common feed. The model results will be
compared with the corresponding at-scale records for centrate turbidity, clarified
harvest turbidity, step recovery, and the HCP and DNA content of the clarified harvest.
The acceptance criteria for that comparison are given below (§7). The qualification
report will be issued before the characterization runs begin and will be summarized in
PCR-004.

The model has a known limitation. It reproduces the sedimentation and filtration duty of
the commercial train, but it does not reproduce the residence time distribution of the
commercial bowl or the frequency of its solids discharge. Confirmation at commercial
scale comes from the turbidity and recovery records of the PPQ batches, and this
limitation will be restated in the report.

## Operation

The broth will be harvested at the end of the fed-batch culture, at the nominal end of
culture viability of `{python} f"{V['final_viability_pct']:.0f}"`% for the platform
process and at a nominal titre of `{python} f"{V['nominal_titer_g_per_l']:.2f}"` g/L
(PCP-003). Broth is fed continuously to the centrifuge (SOP-2005). The centrate passes to
the graded depth filter train and then to a sterilising grade filter (SOP-2006). The
clarified harvest is collected, sampled and held for capture.

Two feed states will be used, because the solids load and the lysis-derived impurity
burden both depend on the state of the culture at harvest. The first is a culture
harvested at the nominal duration. The second is a culture harvested after an extended
duration, which has lower viability, a higher solids load and a higher impurity burden,
and which is the worst case that the clarification train has to handle. The culture
conditions that produce the two feed states are defined in PCP-003.

## Analytical methods

The validated methods are listed in @tbl-sop. Turbidity in the centrate and in the
clarified harvest is measured by nephelometry (AMV-3015). HCP is measured by ELISA
(AMV-3012), residual DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014), and the size variant profile by SEC-HPLC
(AMV-3011).

Method precision sets the smallest difference the study can resolve, so it is stated here
and used again in the decision criteria of §7. The turbidity method has a precision of
`{python} f"{amv_3015_precision:.1f}"`% and a limit of quantitation of
`{python} f"{amv_3015_loq:g}"` NTU. The upper edge of the turbidity operating range
therefore sits about `{python} f"{turb_loq_x:.0f}"` times above the limit of
quantitation, and the whole of the studied range is resolved. The HCP ELISA has a
precision of `{python} f"{amv_3012_precision:.1f}"`%, and a difference in the clarified
harvest burden smaller than that will not be separated from assay variability. Full
method performance is reported in the validations listed in @tbl-sop.

## Sampling plan

Samples will be taken at four points in every run: the bioreactor broth before
centrifugation, the centrate, the pooled depth filtrate, and the clarified harvest after
the sterilising filter (the material released to capture). Turbidity is measured at every
point. HCP, residual DNA and the size variant profile are measured on the broth and on
the clarified harvest, so that the change across the whole step is measured directly and
not inferred from the values recorded at the two intermediate points. Volume and protein
concentration are recorded at each point for the mass balance, and the differential
pressure across the depth filter train is recorded continuously.

## Statistical methods

The analysis is univariate, because no parameter at this step is linked to a critical
quality attribute. Each parameter will be varied across its characterization range while
the other parameters are held at their set-points, and each response will be summarized
as a mean and a standard deviation over the runs executed at that condition on each of
the two feed states. The replicated set-point condition provides the reproducibility term
against which the edge conditions are compared.

Edge conditions will be compared with the set-point condition by a two-sided t-test
(α = 0.05). Statistical significance will be reported separately from practical
significance. A difference that is significant but smaller than the precision of the
method that measured it will be reported as detected and not meaningful, with the method
precision given alongside it.

No response surface model will be fitted, and no design space will be claimed for this
step. Process capability for the attributes in @tbl-cqa is established at the steps that
govern them (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008) and consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

@tbl-params gives the parameters, their set-points, the ranges to be studied, the normal
operating ranges and the study type. The centrifugation set-point of
`{python} setp(p_cent)` and the depth filter load set-point of `{python} setp(p_load)`
are the platform values proposed for commercial operation, and each one is the centre of
its characterization range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO), floatfmt=".0f")
print()
print(": Parameters to be studied, with set-points, characterization ranges, normal "
      "operating ranges and study type. {#tbl-params}")
```

Post-clarification turbidity is not set directly. It is the outcome of the centrifuge and
the depth filter train, and it is the attribute by which the clarified harvest is judged
before it is fed to capture. It appears in @tbl-params because its range defines the feed
that the capture step has to accept, and because it is the in-process control that will
be applied in routine manufacture.

## Univariate assessment

Each settable parameter will be studied at its low characterization edge, at its
set-point and at its high characterization edge, with the other settable parameter held
at its set-point, which gives `{python} n_conditions` clarification conditions in all,
listed in @tbl-cond. Every condition will be run on both feed states. The set-point condition
will be run in triplicate on each feed state, and it is the reference for every
comparison.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cond_df)
print()
print(": Planned univariate conditions. Each condition is run on both feed states; the "
      "set-point condition is run in triplicate. {#tbl-cond}")
```

Two corners of the studied region are worst cases, for opposite reasons. The low
centrifugation and high filter load corner carries the largest solids burden into a
filter train that is already near the end of its capacity, and it is expected to give the
highest turbidity in the clarified harvest and the highest differential pressure across
the depth filters. The high centrifugation corner gives the clearest centrate but the
greatest shear, and it is the condition at which the lysis-derived HCP and DNA burden is
expected to be highest. Both corners will be run on the extended culture feed state.

The turbidity range will be spanned by these conditions, and, where the conditions do not
reach the edges of the range, by blending clarified harvest to the required turbidity.
Material at the low, set-point and high end of the turbidity range will be retained for
the capture feed challenge described in PCP-005.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

@tbl-acc gives the criteria that each studied condition has to meet. Three of them are
process performance criteria (turbidity, recovery and filter train pressure). The other
two confirm that the step does not alter product quality and that the impurity burden
handed to capture is characterized.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(acc_df)
print()
print(": Acceptance and decision criteria for a studied condition. {#tbl-acc}")
```

Product recovery is the criterion with the largest consequence for the process. The
platform recovery over this step is `{python} pct(y_base)` with a batch-to-batch
coefficient of variation of `{python} pct(y_cv)`, so a condition will be judged to have
reduced recovery when its mean falls below `{python} pct(y_floor)`, which is three
standard deviations below the platform mean. Turbidity in the clarified harvest has to
remain inside its normal operating range at the set-point condition, and it is reported
without a limit at the other conditions.

A condition that fails a criterion does not invalidate the study. The proven acceptable
range of that parameter is narrowed to the last level that met every criterion, and the
narrowed range is carried into PCR-004 together with the evidence for it. A failure at
the set-point condition, or a failure of the scale-down model qualification, stops the
study and is escalated under the quality system.

The scale-down model qualification will be accepted when the model and at-scale values of
centrate turbidity, clarified harvest turbidity and step recovery agree within the
precision of the methods that measure them, and when the HCP and DNA content of the
clarified harvest produced by the model falls inside the range recorded at commercial
scale. If the model fails on any of these, it will be modified and requalified before any
characterization run is executed.

The study is complete when every condition in @tbl-cond has been executed on both feed
states, every planned sample has been assayed, the mass balance has been closed, and the
criteria in @tbl-acc have been evaluated for each condition.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

The proven acceptable ranges for this step will be derived from process performance and
not from a drug substance specification. No critical quality attribute is formed or
cleared here, so there is no attribute limit from which a step level criterion could be
back-calculated (as it is for the viral clearance steps). The acceptance basis is the set
of criteria in @tbl-acc, together with the requirement that the clarified harvest is
acceptable as feed to the capture step.

For each settable parameter, the proven acceptable range will be the contiguous interval
around the set-point over which every criterion in @tbl-acc is met on both feed states,
and it will be read from the univariate series and reported next to the full
characterization range so that the margin between the two is visible. Where every studied
level meets the criteria, the whole characterization range will be reported as proven
acceptable, and the binding constraint on routine operation will remain the normal
operating range.

Two analyses that a multivariate step would report will not be run here. There is no
fitted response surface model, so a proven acceptable range cannot be propagated by
Monte-Carlo simulation of the other parameters varying within their normal operating
ranges. There is no multivariate operating region either, so no design space is claimed
for the step. The proven acceptable ranges reported for harvest and clarification will be
univariate, and they will hold for the two feed states studied and at the qualified
scale-down model.

Each proven acceptable range will be presented as a plot of the response against the
parameter, with the acceptance criterion drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and
the set-point and the normal operating range marked. The plots and the data behind them
will be given in the report (PCR-004).

# Data management and integrity

Study data will be recorded and reviewed under the ALCOA+ principles. Raw analytical data
are captured in the validated laboratory systems named in the method validations
(@tbl-sop), and process data are captured in the scale-down model batch records. Each
record is reviewed by a second qualified person before the data are used in the report.
Changes to an executed record are made by controlled amendment with the reason recorded.

# Roles and responsibilities

Process Development prepares this plan, executes the scale-down runs and authors PCR-004.
Analytical Development performs the assays and releases the results against the validated
methods. MSAT owns the scale-down model qualification and the comparison with the
at-scale records (§5.1). Statistics reviews the analysis and the decision rules. Quality
Assurance approves the plan and the report and dispositions any deviation.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable is PCR-004, the process characterization report for this step
(@tbl-related). The work runs in three phases. Scale-down model qualification is executed
and reported first. The characterization runs on the two feed states follow, with the
analytical testing and the mass balance closed out as each condition completes. The
report is then authored, reviewed and approved, and it rolls up into PCMR-001. No dates
are given in this synthetic plan.

# Risks and assumptions

The main risk to the study is the representativeness of the scale-down model. The model is
qualified against at-scale records before use, and its limitation (§5.1) is carried into
the report.

The second risk is the supply of the extended culture feed state, which depends on the
bioreactor campaign run under PCP-003, and if that material is not available the
worst-case conditions will be executed on the nominal feed state and the gap stated in
PCR-004 as a bound on the conclusions.

The study assumes that the platform centrifuge and the platform depth filter media are
unchanged for commercial manufacture. It also assumes that the impurity burden of the
clarified harvest is set by the culture and not by the clarification train. The HCP and
DNA measurements taken across the step will test that second assumption directly.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when the approvals recorded in @tbl-appr are complete. Changes
after approval are made by controlled revision. Any departure from the plan during
execution is recorded at the time and assessed in PCR-004.
